mainTopic: When a baby recognizes his mother, how long a child may nurse, and related laws of human milk and nursing
overview: The גמרא asks how old a baby must be before we assume he recognizes his mother, so that a divorced mother cannot refuse to nurse him. רב says three months, שמואל thirty days, and רבי יוחנן fifty days, and the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן. רמי בר יחזקאל reports that שמואל actually set no age: it depends on whether this baby recognizes her. A story shows שמואל having a baby tested, and רב אשי explains that a blind baby recognizes his mother by smell and taste. A ברייתא then records how long a child may nurse: רבי אליעזר says twenty-four months, and רבי יהושע says even four or five years, and the הלכה follows רבי יהושע. The גמרא explains that human milk that has left the body is permitted, and only nursing directly at an older age is like a שקץ. Blood works the opposite way. Two related שבת rulings follow, where the רבנן did not forbid an unusual way of doing a מלאכה in a case of pain or loss. The גמרא sets a three-day break as counting for weaning, and it begins a ברייתא saying that a nursing widow may not remarry within twenty-four months.

steps.title: How old must the baby be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what age we assume a baby already recognizes his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until how old?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how old a baby must be before we say he recognizes his mother. This question sets up the opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion said that a divorced mother must keep nursing a baby who recognizes her, because separating them could put the baby in danger. Now the גמרא wants a clear age for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Until how much? (here: until what age?)

phrases.english: Until how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how old must the baby be before we assume he knows his mother?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which a baby is assumed to recognize his mother.

steps.title: Three opinions: three months, thirty days, fifty days
steps.stepSummary: רב says three months, שמואל says thirty days, and רבי יוחנן says fifty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא, who said in the name of רב: three months. שמואל said: thirty days. רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: fifty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three different answers to the question of the baby's age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא gives a fixed number. They all agree that a baby needs some time before he recognizes his mother. They disagree only on how long that takes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
Three months,
and Shmuel said: Thirty days.
And Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Fifty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with three opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: three months; שמואל: thirty days; רבי יוחנן: fifty days.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן: fifty days
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אביי rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן's fifty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אביי said: The הלכה follows what רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא decides the practical הלכה among the three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifty-day view becomes the practical rule. This ruling is given before the גמרא goes on to question שמואל's view.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: The halacha is like what Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, a baby of fifty days is assumed to recognize his mother.

steps.title: Can a one-month-old really recognize his mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands the gap between רב and רבי יוחנן, but questions whether thirty days, as שמואל says, is realistic.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רב and רבי יוחנן: each one depends on the baby's sharpness. But according to שמואל, can you really find a case like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's opinion. Fifty days or three months sound reasonable, but a thirty-day-old baby who knows his mother seems hard to believe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babies develop at different speeds, so some may know their mother at fifty days and others only at three months. That explains the gap between רב and רבי יוחנן. Thirty days, though, seems too young for any baby.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (sets up a contrast)
Can you find such a case?

phrases.english: Granted, Rav and Rabbi Yochanan:
each and every one according to his sharpness.
phrases.notes: Each baby is different. A sharp one knows his mother sooner, so both numbers can be true.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ?
phrases.english: can you find a case like this?
phrases.notes: "Like this" means a baby only thirty days old who already knows his mother.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Babies' sharpness can explain fifty days versus three months, but thirty days seems too early for any baby.

steps.title: שמואל never set an age: it depends on the baby
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל says the thirty-day report is wrong. שמואל ruled that it depends on whether this baby actually recognizes his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רמי בר יחזקאל came, he said: Don't listen to these rules that my brother יהודה stated in the name of שמואל. This is what שמואל said: whenever the baby recognizes her.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by correcting the report of שמואל's view. שמואל did not say thirty days. He said to check each baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with thirty days goes away because שמואל never set a number at all. In his view, the test is a fact about the individual baby: does he recognize his mother or not?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל, אָמַר:
phrases.english: When Rami bar Yechezkel came, he said:
Do not listen to these rules
that my brother Yehuda set down in the name of Shmuel.
This is what Shmuel said:
Whenever he recognizes her.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the report of שמואל's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל set a fixed age of thirty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל set no age. It depends on whether the baby actually recognizes his mother.

steps.title: שמואל has a baby tested in a row of women
steps.stepSummary: A divorced woman comes before שמואל. רב דימי בר יוסף tests whether her baby knows her, and the baby happily picks her out.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before שמואל. He told רב דימי בר יוסף: Go check her. He went and sat her in a row of women, took her son, and carried him past them. When he reached her, the baby looked at her face with joy, and she turned her eyes away from him. He said to her: Lift up your eyes, get up and take your son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows שמואל's "check each baby" approach being used in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of counting days, שמואל has the baby tested. The baby's joyful reaction proves he recognizes his mother, so she must take him and nurse him.

phrases.english: A certain woman came before Shmuel.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: He said to Rav Dimi bar Yosef:
Go check her.
He went and sat her in a row of women,
and took her son
and passed him around by them.
When he reached her,
he was looking at her face with joy,
and she lowered her eyes away from him.
He said to her: Lift up your eyes,
get up and carry your son.

steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that recognition depends on testing the individual baby
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story in which שמואל ordered a practical test of the baby

steps.title: How does a blind baby recognize his mother?
steps.stepSummary: If recognition means seeing her face, how could a blind baby ever recognize his mother?
steps.simpleTranslation: A blind baby, how does he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the story's test: it relies on sight, so what about a blind baby?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If recognizing means seeing, a blind baby would never count as recognizing his mother. The mother of a blind baby could then always refuse to nurse him. The גמרא wants to know how that case works.

phrases.english: A blind one, how does he know?

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that recognition is based on sight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blind baby cannot see his mother's face, so how could he ever recognize her?

steps.title: Through smell and taste
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a blind baby recognizes his mother by her smell and the taste of her milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: by smell and by taste.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question about the blind baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Recognition does not have to come through the eyes. A baby can know his mother through other senses, so the rule applies to a blind baby too.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Through smell and through taste.

steps.terutzMaskana: Recognition can come through smell and taste, so a blind baby can also recognize his mother.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is fifty days, as רבי יוחנן said. According to רמי בר יחזקאל's report, שמואל held that it depends on whether the baby actually recognizes his mother, even by smell and taste.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: nursing only until 24 months
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says a child may nurse until twenty-four months. After that, it is like nursing from a non-kosher creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A child may keep nursing until twenty-four months. From then on, he is like one who nurses from a non-kosher creature. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic connected to nursing: how long a child may keep nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר sets a firm limit of twenty-four months. After that point, nursing is treated like eating from something forbidden.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A child continues to nurse
until twenty-four months;
from here on, he is like one who nurses from a non-kosher creature,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nursing is permitted until twenty-four months. After that, it is like nursing from a non-kosher creature.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: even four or five years, unless he stopped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע allows nursing even for four or five years. A child who stopped after twenty-four months and then went back is like one nursing from a non-kosher creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Even four or five years. If he stopped after twenty-four months and then went back, he is like one who nurses from a non-kosher creature.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע disagrees with רבי אליעזר and allows a much longer nursing period, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, what matters is whether the nursing continued without a break, not the child's age. If the child stopped after twenty-four months, going back to nursing is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: The last line (stopped after twenty-four months and went back) is part of רבי יהושע's view. It is not רבי אליעזר's. רבי אליעזר forbids all nursing after twenty-four months anyway.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Even four or five years.

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירַשׁ לְאַחַר עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חֹדֶשׁ וְחָזַר —
phrases.english: If he stopped after twenty-four months and went back,
he is like one who nurses from a non-kosher creature.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אַרְבַּע וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר's twenty-four-month limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Continuous nursing is permitted even for four or five years. Going back to nursing after stopping past twenty-four months is forbidden.

steps.title: Contradiction: a ברייתא suggests human milk might be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'like nursing from a שקץ' and starts a contradiction from another ברייתא. That ברייתא opens with a קל וחומר that seems to show human milk should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: after twenty-four months it is like nursing from a non-kosher creature. But a ברייתא raises a contradiction. You might think human milk is forbidden. A non-kosher animal does not make things impure by touch while it is alive, yet its milk is forbidden. A person does make things impure by touch, so shouldn't his milk be forbidden even more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the line 'like nursing from a שקץ' and starts to set up a contradiction from a different ברייתא. This step only gives the ברייתא's first idea. The rest of the contradiction comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first builds a קל וחומר. An animal is lenient about touch but strict about milk, and a person is strict about touch. So it seems a person should be strict about milk too. This is only the 'you might think' stage, and the ברייתא will reject it next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', which brings back a line from an earlier source
'And they raised a contradiction', setting one source against another
'Those who walk on two legs', meaning human beings
'It is logical', which introduces a reasoning argument like a קל וחומר
Touch, contact (here, passing on impurity by touch)

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע we just learned.

phrases.english: From here on, it is like nursing from a non-kosher creature.
And they raised a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא חֲלֵב מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם טָמֵא.
phrases.english: You might think the milk of two-legged ones is impure.
And it is logical:
If an animal, where you were lenient about its touch,
phrases.notes: He means a non-kosher animal, which does not make things impure by touch while it is alive.

phrases.english: you were strict about its milk,
then a person, where you were strict about his touch,
isn't it logical that you should be strict about his milk?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the phrase 'כיונק שקץ' from steps 9–10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that nursing past twenty-four months is like nursing from a שקץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא will conclude that human milk is permitted. Calling it like a שקץ seems to clash with that.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that human milk and human blood are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר. The extra word 'הוא' in the פסוק about the camel teaches that only the camel is forbidden. Human milk is permitted, and so is human blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'the camel, because it chews the cud, it is impure.' 'It' is impure, but human milk is not impure; it is permitted. You might think: I can leave out milk, since not everyone has it, but not blood, which everyone has. So the פסוק says 'it': it is impure, but human blood is not impure; it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its argument. A word in the פסוק shows that human milk is permitted, and even human blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוא' limits the prohibition to the animal itself and leaves out things from humans. The ברייתא then asks whether blood might be stricter, since all people have blood but only women have milk. The same word 'הוא' leaves out human blood as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches', which brings a פסוק to settle the question
'It', a limiting word here: only 'it' is forbidden
The same in everyone (all people have blood, but only women have milk)
Literally 'pure'; here it means permitted to eat

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא, 'טמא' and 'טהור' mean forbidden and permitted to eat. They do not mean impure or pure in the sense of touching.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic הלכה: on a Torah level, human milk is a permitted food.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"The camel, because it chews the cud"
it is impure,
but the milk of two-legged ones is not impure,
rather, it is pure.
You might think I should leave out milk,
which is not the same in everyone,
but I should not leave out blood,
which is the same in everyone.
So the verse says "it":
it is impure,
but the blood of two-legged ones is not impure,
rather, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradicting ברייתא by rejecting its first idea with a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human milk and human blood are permitted on a Torah level, learned from the word 'הוא'.

steps.title: רב ששת: not even a מצוה to stay away from human milk
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds that there is not even a מצוה to keep away from human milk. This makes the contradiction with 'like a שקץ' even sharper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: there is not even a מצוה to stay away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת makes the contradiction stronger. Human milk is permitted, and there is not even a מצוה to avoid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רב ששת, someone could say human milk is permitted but still something to avoid. רב ששת closes that door. So how can nursing be compared to a שקץ?

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה to stay away from something, even if it is not forbidden

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
There is not even a מצוה to stay away from it.
phrases.notes: "It" means human milk, which the ברייתא just said is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the ברייתא of step 12 and sharpens the contradiction begun in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human milk has no prohibition at all, not even a מצוה to stay away from it.

steps.title: Milk that left the body versus nursing directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא permitting human milk is talking about milk that has left the body. Calling it 'like a שקץ' is about nursing straight from the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. One source is talking about milk that has left the body. The other is talking about milk that has not left the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by showing that each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milk itself is permitted, as the ברייתא and רב ששת said. But an older child nursing directly from a woman is what is compared to nursing from a שקץ. That way both sources are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult', which opens an answer to a contradiction
Separated, meaning the milk has left the body
'This ... that', splitting the two sources into two different cases

steps.whatToRemember: Human milk is permitted on a Torah level, and there is not even a מצוה to avoid it. Only nursing directly from a woman after twenty-four months is compared to nursing from a שקץ.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where it has separated,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא and רב ששת: milk that already came out of the woman's body is fine.

phrases.english: that is where it has not separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּפָרֵישׁ, הָא דְּלָא פָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 11–13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that 'like a שקץ' meant human milk itself is forbidden, which would clash with the ברייתא and רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Milk that has left the body is fully permitted. Nursing directly at an older age is what is compared to a שקץ.

steps.title: Blood works the opposite way from milk
steps.stepSummary: Human blood that left the body is forbidden, but blood still in the body is allowed. A ברייתא supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the opposite is true for blood. As a ברייתא teaches: blood on a loaf of bread, you scrape it off and then eat the bread. Blood between your teeth, you may suck it and not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that human blood follows the reverse rule of human milk, and it brings a ברייתא to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With milk, milk that has left the body is allowed, but nursing straight from the woman is 'like a שקץ'. Blood is the reverse. Blood that has left the body, like blood on bread, is forbidden by the רבנן and must be scraped off. Blood that never left the body, like blood between the teeth, may be swallowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. For milk, milk out of the body is fine. For blood, blood out of the body is the forbidden one.

phrases.english: And the opposite applies to blood.
phrases.notes: With blood, what left the body is forbidden and what is still inside is allowed. That is the reverse of milk.

phrases.english: As it is taught: blood that is on a loaf of bread —
he scrapes it off and eats it.
phrases.notes: He scrapes off the blood and then eats the bread.

phrases.english: blood that is between the teeth —
he sucks it and need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer of step 14 by applying the same in-body/out-of-body distinction to blood, in reverse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Human blood that left the body is forbidden by the רבנן, and blood still in the mouth is allowed.

steps.title: Two quotes from רבי יהושע about nursing age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יהושע's 'four or five years' and points to another ברייתא where he says 'even with his bundle on his shoulders.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהושע says, even four or five years. But another ברייתא teaches that רבי יהושע says: even when the child carries his bundle on his shoulders!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהושע's statement from step 10 and asks why another ברייתא quotes him with a different measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא gives a number of years. The other gives a picture: a child old enough to carry a load. It looks like the two quotes give רבי יהושע different limits, so the גמרא asks which one he really said.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; used to go back and look at a line from an earlier source
But isn't it taught? This opens a contradiction

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: We are going back to the ברייתא from step 10.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
even four or five years.
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
even when his bundle is on his shoulders!
phrases.notes: He means the child is old enough to carry a load and may still nurse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the blood/milk topic and returns to the nursing-age statement from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's statement 'even four or five years' (step 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא quotes רבי יהושע with a different measure, 'his bundle on his shoulders,' so the two reports seem to conflict.

steps.title: Both quotes describe the same age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'four or five years' and 'bundle on his shoulders' are the same measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one and that one are one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two quotes are two ways of describing the same age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child of four or five is about the age when he can carry a bundle on his shoulders. So the two ברייתות only use different words. They do not disagree.

phrases.english: This and that
are one measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: the two statements are the same measure in different words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two quotes give רבי יהושע two different age limits.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both describe the same age, so there is no disagreement.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע on nursing age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the practical ruling on how long a child may nurse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We follow רבי יהושע's view, which is the most lenient one. A child may keep nursing until about four or five years old.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the rulings in this section
The practical law follows the view of...

steps.whatToRemember: Human milk out of the body is allowed. Blood out of the body is forbidden. A child may nurse until about four or five years old, like רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling after the contradiction was resolved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע on the age limit for nursing.

steps.title: A sick person may suck milk on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי מרינוס teaches that a sick person who needs milk may suck it straight from an animal on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מרינוס says, a person who is sick and groaning may suck milk on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, still on the topic of sucking milk, about a sick person on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milking an animal is normally a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. רבי מרינוס allows a sick person who needs milk to suck it straight from the animal with his mouth. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
The תנא who gives this ruling
One who groans, a sick person who needs milk

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Marinos says:
One who is groaning from illness —
may suck milk on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic about sucking milk, now in the context of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick person who needs milk may suck it directly from an animal on שבת.

steps.title: Why sucking milk is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Sucking is milking in an unusual way, which is only forbidden by the רבנן, and they did not forbid it when someone is in pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Sucking is taking out the milk in an unusual way, and when there is pain the רבנן did not make a גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מרינוס allows this and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milking falls under the מלאכה of מפרק, taking something out of where it is held. Doing it with the mouth is not the normal way, so the Torah does not forbid it. Only the רבנן do, and they did not forbid it when a person is in pain.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking something out of its holder; milking belongs to this מלאכה
In an unusual way, literally 'with the back of the hand'

phrases.english: What is the reason?
One who sucks is extracting in an unusual way,
and in a case of pain
the Rabbis did not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא: יוֹנֵק מְפָרֵק כִּלְאַחַר יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי מרינוס's ruling in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is sucking milk allowed on שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a מלאכה done in an unusual way, which is only forbidden by the רבנן, and they did not forbid it when someone is in pain.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי מרינוס
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the הלכה follows רבי מרינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the הלכה follows רבי מרינוס.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the practical ruling about the sick person sucking milk on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a sick person who needs milk may suck it straight from an animal on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows רבי מרינוס

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Marinos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מָרִינוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on step 19's case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי מרינוס: a sick person may suck milk from an animal on שבת.

steps.title: Crushing weeds in a blocked drainpipe on שבת
steps.stepSummary: נחום איש גליא teaches that one may quietly crush weeds blocking a drainpipe with his foot on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: נחום איש גליא says, if weeds grew up in a drainpipe, a person may crush them with his foot privately on שבת, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that works the same way as רבי מרינוס's case, this time about a blocked pipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearing a blocked pipe fixes it, and fixing an item is normally a מלאכה on שבת. נחום איש גליא allows crushing the weeds with the foot, done privately. The next step gives the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: נחום from the place called גליא, the תנא of this ruling
In private, not in public view

phrases.english: It is taught: Nachum of Galia says:
A drainpipe in which weeds grew up —
he crushes them with his foot
in private on Shabbat, and he need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to רבי מרינוס's: an unusual way of doing a מלאכה is allowed in a special situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may crush weeds blocking a drainpipe with his foot, privately, on שבת.

steps.title: Why crushing the weeds is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Fixing with the foot is an unusual way of fixing, and the רבנן did not forbid it when there would be a money loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is fixing in an unusual way, and when there is a loss the רבנן did not make a גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why נחום איש גליא allows this, using the same reasoning as in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixing an item with your foot is not the usual way, so it is only forbidden by the רבנן. Here the reason they did not forbid it is to prevent a loss. Step 20 used pain as the reason. Here it is loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixing or repairing an item, a שבת מלאכה

phrases.english: What is the reason?
it is fixing in an unusual way,
and in a case of loss
the Rabbis did not make a decree about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא — מְתַקֵּן כִּלְאַחַר יָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains step 22 with the same logic as step 20, replacing pain with financial loss.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why may one crush the weeds on שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is fixing in an unusual way, which is only forbidden by the רבנן, and they did not forbid it where there is a loss.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like נחום איש גליא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the הלכה follows נחום איש גליא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the הלכה follows נחום איש גליא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the practical ruling about the blocked drainpipe, which closes this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, one may crush the weeds with his foot, privately, on שבת. This is the third time in a row that רב יוסף rules like the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows נחום איש גליא

steps.whatToRemember: A מלאכה done כלאחר יד is only forbidden by the רבנן. They did not apply their גזירה when there is pain (sucking milk) or money loss (crushing weeds in a pipe). רב יוסף rules like both of these lenient views.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two cases show a general rule for שבת: some rabbinic גזירות were not applied in cases of pain or loss.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halacha is like Nachum of Galia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּנַחוּם אִישׁ גַּלְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on step 22's case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows נחום איש גליא: one may crush weeds blocking a drainpipe with his foot on שבת.

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: a child who stopped nursing and went back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the ברייתא's ruling: a child who stopped nursing after twenty-four months and then went back is like someone nursing from a forbidden creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a child stopped nursing after twenty-four months and then went back, he is like one who nurses from a שקץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion is over, and the גמרא returns to the line from the ברייתא it was learning. It quotes that line again to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before twenty-four months, a child may nurse. Once a child older than twenty-four months has stopped, going back is treated like drinking from a forbidden source. The question this raises is: how long a break counts as truly stopping?

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who nurses from a forbidden creature
Twenty-four months, the normal nursing period

phrases.english: If he stopped after twenty-four months
phrases.notes: "He" is the nursing child from the ברייתא we learned before the side discussion.

phrases.english: and then went back, he is like one who nurses from a forbidden creature.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירַשׁ לְאַחַר עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חֹדֶשׁ וְחָזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussions (human milk and blood, the two quotes of רבי יהושע, and the שבת cases in steps 11-24) to the last line of the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child who stopped nursing after twenty-four months and went back is treated like one nursing from a שקץ.

steps.title: How long a break counts as stopping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the child must stop nursing before going back is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ruling it just quoted. It wants to know how long the break must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says "stopped" but gives no amount of time. A child may skip nursing for a few hours, so the גמרא needs a clear line for when it counts as fully stopping.

phrases.english: And how long?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how long must he stop nursing before going back counts as forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time length behind the word פֵּירַשׁ in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long a break in nursing counts as stopping.

steps.title: שמואל: three days
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר חביבא says in the name of שמואל that the break is three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר חביבא said in the name of שמואל: three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A break of three days counts as stopping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a child older than twenty-four months has gone three days without nursing, he counts as weaned. If he goes back after that, it is like nursing from a שקץ. A shorter break does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports this from שמואל

steps.whatToRemember: A child older than twenty-four months who stops nursing for three days may not go back.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Ḥaviva said
that Shmuel said: Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר חֲבִיבָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A three-day break counts as stopping.

steps.title: Another version: the three days was a ברייתא taught before שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Some say the three-day rule was not שמואל's own words. רב יהודה בר חביבא taught it as a ברייתא in front of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב יהודה בר חביבא taught in front of שמואל: three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who said the three-day rule. The rule stays the same; only the source changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, it is שמואל's own ruling. In this version, it is an older teaching (תני) recited in front of שמואל, which would give it the weight of a ברייתא. Either way, the answer is three days.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught
before Shmuel: Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, תָּנֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר חֲבִיבָא קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of who said the answer in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three days, recorded as a ברייתא taught in front of שמואל.

steps.title: New ברייתא: a nursing widow may not remarry yet
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a nursing woman whose husband died within twenty-four months of the birth may not get engaged or married.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A nursing woman whose husband died within twenty-four months may not get engaged and may not get married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about nursing. It quotes a ברייתא saying that a nursing widow must wait before getting engaged or married again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now move from the child to the mother. Because she is still nursing within the twenty-four months, she may not get engaged (אירוסין) or married (נישואין). The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And she may not get married (נישואין)

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A nursing woman
whose husband died
within twenty-four months,
she may not get engaged
and may not get married

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the twenty-four-month nursing period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nursing widow within twenty-four months of the birth may not get engaged or married.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the rule that a nursing widow must wait before remarrying.
